mobile.sidebar.view_options.note: Accessible name of the small sliders icon beside the drawer's search pill, and the title of the compact sheet it opens. Mirrors the desktop's 'View options' (ui.chat.sidebar.header.view_options).

mobile.sidebar.order_by.note: Label of the choice of how conversations are ordered in the drawer. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.order_by.

mobile.sidebar.order.active_first.note: Order option: conversations with a turn running, or waiting on the reader, are lifted to the top; the rest follow newest first. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.active_first.

mobile.sidebar.order.most_recent.note: Order option: one newest-first order over every conversation, nothing lifted. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.most_recent.

mobile.sidebar.group_by.note: Label of the choice of how the drawer groups conversations. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.group_by.

mobile.sidebar.group.time_section.note: Grouping option: headed sections Pinned, Running, Today, This week, Older. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.time_section.

mobile.sidebar.group.one_list.note: Grouping option: one list with no section headings. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.one_list.

mobile.sidebar.group.tag.note: Grouping option: one group per tag, pinned conversations first and untagged last. Only offered on a relay with the tag registry. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.tag.

mobile.sidebar.time_basis.note: Label of the choice of which clock the sections, the row times and the order read. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.time_basis.

mobile.sidebar.basis.last_active.note: Clock option: when the conversation last had activity. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.last_active.

mobile.sidebar.basis.created.note: Clock option: when the conversation was started. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.created.

mobile.sidebar.clock_hint.note: One sentence under the clock choice explaining that it changes both the dates shown and the order. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.clock_hint.

mobile.sidebar.show_ended.note: Switch label: whether conversations whose session has ended stay in the drawer. Phone-only setting; on by default.

mobile.sidebar.show_ended_hint.note: One sentence under the 'Show ended sessions' switch: turning it off never hides a pinned or running conversation.

mobile.sidebar.show_tags.note: Switch label: whether each conversation row paints its tag line in the drawer. On by default; a relay without the tag routes never shows the switch.

mobile.sidebar.show_tags_hint.note: One sentence under the 'Show tags' switch: turning the line off does not remove anything, because the tags sheet in each conversation's long-press menu still assigns them.

mobile.sidebar.sections.note: Label of the list of switches that show or hide each drawer section. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.sections.

mobile.sidebar.section.pinned.note: Drawer section heading for conversations the reader pinned; also the switch label that shows or hides it. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.section.pinned.

mobile.sidebar.section.running.note: Drawer section heading for conversations with a turn in flight or waiting on the reader. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.section.running.

mobile.sidebar.section.today.note: Drawer section heading for conversations from this local calendar day. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.section.today.

mobile.sidebar.section.week.note: Drawer section heading for conversations from the last six calendar days, not today. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.section.week.

mobile.sidebar.section.older.note: Drawer section heading for everything older than this week. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.section.older.

mobile.sidebar.section.untagged.note: Drawer section heading under the Tag grouping for conversations whose primary tag is unset. Not a switch label; the tag grouping has no per-section switches.

mobile.sidebar.tag_group.announcement.note: Screen-reader name of a tag group's heading. {name} is the operator's own tag name (or the word Untagged) and must not be translated here; the ICU plural says how many conversations the group holds and keeps the `#` placeholder.

mobile.sidebar.more_settings.note: Link at the foot of the drawer's View options sheet that opens the full Sidebar section in Settings.

mobile.sidebar.settings_heading.note: Heading of the Settings section holding every drawer (sidebar) view option.

mobile.sidebar.hidden_sections.note: Quiet line at the top of the drawer's list when the reader has switched sections off in Settings → Sidebar; {count} is a number. Preserve ICU plural arms and #. Desktop: ui.chat.sidebar_view.hidden.

mobile.sidebar.empty_by_view.headline.note: Empty-state headline in the drawer when conversations exist but the reader's view options (hidden sections, Show ended sessions off) hide every one of them. Not 'no conversations'.

mobile.sidebar.empty_by_view.next.note: Second line of that empty state: names the ways back. 'Sections' are Pinned/Running/Today/This week/Older; 'ended sessions' is the Show ended sessions switch.

mobile.sidebar.empty_by_view.reset.note: Action of that empty state: restores the default drawer view (every section shown, ended sessions shown, default order and grouping).

mobile.sidebar.outbox_sending.note: Small line on a conversation row in the conversation list while the phone is still delivering a message the user sent to that conversation (retrying in the background). Also read aloud as part of the row.

mobile.sidebar.outbox_failed.note: Small line in danger colour on a conversation row in the conversation list when the phone stopped trying to deliver a message to that conversation and needs the user (Retry or Discard inside the conversation). Delivery is UNKNOWN: must not claim the message was definitely not received. Also read aloud as part of the row.

mobile.sidebar.tags.remove_all.note: Destructive button in the conversation Tags sheet that clears every category from this conversation (opens a confirm). Keep under ~24 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.remove_all_title.note: Title of the confirm dialog opened by Remove all tags. Question, keep under ~28 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.remove_all_body.note: Body of the Remove all tags confirm dialog: the assignment is cleared, the categories are not deleted. Two sentences. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.remove_all_confirm.note: Destructive confirm button of the Remove all tags dialog. One verb, keep under ~12 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.saving.note: Muted progress word shown beside a tag row (and under Remove all tags) while the write is in flight. Keep the single ellipsis character. Keep under ~12 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.load_failed_title.note: Title of the error alert in the Tags sheet when the category list could not be read. No final period. Keep under ~32 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.load_failed_body.note: Body of the error alert in the Tags sheet; a pinned Try again button follows. Two short sentences, blameless. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.empty_headline.note: Empty-state headline in the Tags sheet when no tag categories exist. Short sentence, keep under ~28 characters; shown at 200% text in a ~300 pt sheet. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.empty_next.note: Empty-state second line in the Tags sheet: categories are created in the desktop app, not on the phone. Very short (the 200% frame cut a longer line); keep under ~24 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.tags.announcement.note: Screen-reader name of a conversation row's tag line. {names} is the operator's own category names joined with ", " (user data, never translated). Keep the placeholder; the "Tags" word should match relay.chrome.row.tags.

mobile.sidebar.row.new.note: Accent marker on a conversation row with unread activity. One lowercase word, keep under ~8 characters (sits in a crowded meta strip). No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row.asks.note: Count chip on a conversation row: open asks (questions/approvals queued for the operator). Monospace meta strip, never truncated: keep each arm under ~10 characters. ICU plural with `#` for the number; keep the `one` and `other` arms and add the locale's own CLDR arms (few/many) where it has them.

mobile.sidebar.row.asks_not_blocker.note: Screen-reader name of the asks chip. {asks} is the already-formatted count (mobile.sidebar.row.asks, e.g. "2 asks"); "not a blocker" says the agent keeps working, it is NOT waiting. Keep the placeholder.

mobile.sidebar.row.agents.note: Count chip on a conversation row: running subagents. Monospace meta strip that yields at large text; keep each arm under ~10 characters. ICU plural with `#` for the number; keep the `one` and `other` arms and add the locale's own CLDR arms (few/many) where it has them.

mobile.sidebar.row.todos.note: Count chip on a conversation row: open todo items in the conversation's task list. Monospace meta strip that yields at large text; keep each arm under ~10 characters. ICU plural with `#` for the number; keep the `one` and `other` arms and add the locale's own CLDR arms (few/many) where it has them.

mobile.sidebar.menu.pin.note: Row in the long-press menu of a conversation in the sidebar: keeps this conversation at the top of the list. Short action, no final full stop.

mobile.sidebar.menu.unpin.note: Row in the long-press menu of a conversation that is already pinned: removes it from the top of the list. Short action, no final full stop.

mobile.sidebar.menu.move.note: Row in the long-press menu of a conversation: opens a sheet to move or copy the conversation to another computer. The ellipsis says another step follows; keep it.

mobile.sidebar.menu.tags.note: Row in the long-press menu of a conversation: opens a sheet to assign the conversation's tags (categories created on desktop). The ellipsis says another step follows; keep it.

mobile.sidebar.menu.open.note: Last row in the long-press menu of a conversation: opens the conversation, the same as tapping its row. Verb, no final full stop.

mobile.sidebar.empty.search_next.note: Second line under 'Nothing matches that.' when the sidebar search finds no conversation. Explains what the search looks at: the names, ids and folders of the sessions already on screen. 'ids' are session identifiers.

mobile.sidebar.empty.no_route_headline.note: Headline of the sidebar's empty state when the phone is not connected to any computer. Plain statement, not an error.

mobile.sidebar.empty.no_route_next.note: Second line under 'No computer is connected yet.': why a computer is needed. The button below it connects one.

mobile.sidebar.empty.none_headline.note: Headline of the sidebar's empty state when the connected computer has no conversations. A session is one conversation with the agent. Plain statement, not an error.

mobile.sidebar.empty.none_next.note: Second line under 'No sessions yet.': what a session is and what to do next. The 'New chat' button below it starts one.

mobile.sidebar.row.on_device.note: Second line of a conversation row for a conversation running on ANOTHER of the reader's devices (paired over the mesh), in place of the folder/model line local rows show: it names the device the conversation lives on, e.g. "On Studio Mac". Plain, neutral statement of location in the muted row style, sentence case, no final full stop. Width: one line on narrow phone rows (as little as ~200 dp of text at default size), ellipsized at the tail, so keep the words around the name as short as your language allows; the name is what must stay visible. {device} is the device's NAME as the reader chose it (any script, often Latin even in RTL locales): never translate, transliterate, abbreviate or reorder anything inside it; you may move the placeholder within the sentence to suit your grammar (e.g. postposition languages put it first). Urdu (RTL): a Latin device name inside RTL text is bidirectional, so write no bidi control characters; the app lays out direction. Plain text, no ICU arms.

mobile.sidebar.row_status.approval.note: The one status word on a conversation row whose agent is waiting for the reader to approve an action. Painted in the danger colour in a crowded meta strip; one lowercase word, keep under ~10 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_status.question.note: The one status word on a conversation row whose agent asked the reader a question and is waiting for the answer. Painted in the danger colour in a crowded meta strip; one lowercase word, keep under ~10 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_status.not_reachable.note: Muted status word on a row for a conversation on ANOTHER device that the mesh can no longer reach, so the row is stale as a whole. Also read in the row's screen-reader name after the device. Lowercase, keep under ~14 characters; not an error. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_status.ended.note: Muted status word on a row whose conversation has ended (a receipt, not an error). Also read in the row's screen-reader name. One lowercase word, keep under ~10 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_status.not_answering.note: Muted status word on a row whose conversation's runtime is up but has stopped answering (a receipt, not an error). Also read in the row's screen-reader name. Lowercase, keep under ~14 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_label.waiting.note: Fragment of a conversation row's screen-reader name, read after the title when the agent is waiting on the reader: an approval or an answer to a question. Fragments are joined by mobile.sidebar.row_label.join (a comma in English) ("Payments, approval waiting, open"). Keep the select and both arms; translate each arm as a whole phrase, never by composing the status word.

mobile.sidebar.row_label.working.note: Fragment of a conversation row's screen-reader name, read after the title while the agent's turn is running. Fragments are joined by mobile.sidebar.row_label.join (a comma in English). Lowercase, no placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_label.on_device.note: Fragment of a conversation row's screen-reader name for a conversation on another device: {device} is that device's name as the reader set it (e.g. "on Studio Mac"). Fragments are joined by mobile.sidebar.row_label.join (a comma in English). Keep the placeholder; never translate the name.

mobile.sidebar.row_label.open.note: Fragment of a conversation row's screen-reader name, read last when this conversation is the one currently open on screen. Fragments are joined by mobile.sidebar.row_label.join (a comma in English). Lowercase, no placeholders.

mobile.sidebar.row_label.join.note: Separator between two fragments of a conversation row's screen-reader name (never shown on screen; a screen reader speaks it as a pause). {first} is the title or the already-joined fragments so far, {second} is the next fragment, e.g. "Payments, approval waiting, on Studio, open" is built by joining one fragment at a time. A bare list separator: use your locale's enumeration comma and spacing (e.g. full-width or ideographic comma, Arabic-script comma), never a word for "and", no final full stop. Keep both placeholders, {first} before {second}.
